blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Managing a global supply chain means coordinating across time zones, languages, currencies, and local rules — while keeping a single, coherent plan. The work is never finished. A factory in Vietnam closes for Tet. A port in Rotterdam strikes. The euro moves 3% overnight. Each event hits you in a different way, but the response has to feel, to the customer, like one calm organisation.

Two habits keep it together. First, follow the sun: pass live work between teams in different regions so that nothing waits twelve hours for an answer. Second, standardise the language and the templates: when every region uses the same words for the same things, cross-border coordination stops being a translation exercise.

Over a year, these small habits quietly save hundreds of hours and prevent the small misunderstandings that, at scale, become expensive mistakes.

items.q: According to the text, how should the response to disruptions feel to the customer?
items.why: "the response has to feel, to the customer, like one calm organisation."

items.q: What is the purpose of the "follow the sun" habit?
options: To pass live work between regions so nothing waits twelve hours
To keep every decision in one head office
To reduce the number of regional teams
To let each region work only in daylight hours
items.why: "follow the sun: pass live work between teams in different regions so that nothing waits twelve hours for an answer."

items.q: According to the text, standardising the language and templates means that coordination…
items.why: "when every region uses the same words for the same things, cross-border coordination stops being a translation exercise."

items.q: The text suggests that the author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: A supply chain can be set up once and then left alone.
Small habits can add up to large savings over a year.
Local disruptions require a coordinated global response.
items.why: Inferência: o texto abre com "The work is never finished" — o autor discordaria da ideia de deixar a cadeia parada.

items.q: The example of the euro moving 3% overnight suggests that…
options: currency risk is irrelevant to supply chains
prices should be fixed once a year
global coordination must absorb events beyond its control
items.why: Inferência: greves, feriados e câmbio são eventos externos que a organização precisa absorver mantendo um plano coerente.

blocks.instruction: Ouça James explicando ao novo diretor de operações. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Welcome aboard. Let me show you the one thing that holds seven regions together: the Monday morning template. Every regional team fills in exactly the same form, in the same order, using the same words. It looks almost boring — and that is the point.

Before we had it, Singapore would say a shipment was "delayed", London would call it "on hold", and São Paulo would mark it "pending". Three words, one situation, endless confusion. Now, when Tokyo hands the file to Frankfurt at the end of their day, Frankfurt reads it in ninety seconds and keeps moving. Nothing waits twelve hours for someone to wake up.

You will be tempted to let each region tweak the format to suit itself. Please resist that. Standardise the words and the layout — but never the local decision. A port strike in Rotterdam is Rotterdam's call to make; the template just makes sure everyone else hears about it in a form they can act on straight away.

Do this well, and the customer never sees the seams. They see one calm company, even though the sun never sets on the work.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What is the one thing James says holds the seven regions together?
options: A single head office in London
items.why: "the one thing that holds seven regions together: the Monday morning template."

items.q: What problem did the three words "delayed", "on hold" and "pending" cause?
options: They described one situation but created endless confusion
items.why: "Three words, one situation, endless confusion."

items.q: According to James, what should teams standardise — and what should they NOT?
options: Standardise the local decision, not the words
Standardise the words and layout, not the local decision
Standardise the currency, not the layout
items.why: "Standardise the words and the layout — but never the local decision."

items.q: When James says "the customer never sees the seams", he most likely means…
options: the template is hidden from the customer
the customer works in a different time zone
the handovers between regions stay invisible to the customer
the customer never receives a delivery
items.why: Inferência: "seams" são as junções entre as equipes; se o método funciona, o cliente vê uma empresa só.

items.q: Why does James call the template "almost boring", and say "that is the point"?
options: Because he wants a simpler job
Because dull work motivates the teams
Because sameness is exactly what makes fast handovers possible
items.why: Inferência: a repetição sem surpresas é o que permite ler o arquivo em 90 segundos e seguir em frente.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "We keep a single, coherent plan across all regions." Coherent here means…
items.why: Coherent = coerente: as partes se encaixam e formam um todo consistente.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "The dockworkers in Rotterdam voted to ___, so no containers moved for three days."
items.why: To strike = fazer greve — foi por isso que os contêineres pararam.

items.q: "We follow the sun, so a query raised in Tokyo is answered before Europe logs off." Following the sun means…
options: passing live work between regions so it never stops
moving offices closer to the equator
items.why: Follow the sun = seguir o sol: o trabalho passa de fuso em fuso e nunca para.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "When every region uses its own labels, small ___ pile up and become expensive."
items.why: Misunderstanding = mal-entendido; é o que se multiplica com distância e idiomas diferentes.

items.q: "Please standardise the format before you send it on." To standardise means to…
options: make it follow the same fixed pattern
get it approved by a manager
shorten it as much as possible
items.why: To standardise = padronizar: fazer todos seguirem o mesmo modelo e ordem.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões de operações globais. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The regional director has to sign off on the new template before we launch." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We will roll out the Monday template region by region." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva, área por área.

items.q: "Two teams pushed back on using the same labels." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "When Tokyo hands over the file at the end of their day, Frankfurt picks it up." To hand over means to…
items.why: Hand over = passar o trabalho/responsabilidade para outra equipe — a base do follow-the-sun.

items.q: "A shared template really does move the needle on coordination time." This means it…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível.
